newsitem.title: FRANCE: Support for French far right vote of protest - poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for French far right vote of protest - poll.

text.p: A majority of supporters of France's extreme-right National Front vote for the party as a protest against mainstream political organisations, a poll released on Wednesday showed.
Fully 84 percent of the anti-immigrant party's supporters said their votes for its leader, Jean-Marie Le Pen, were born of disillusion with other parties.

Only 30 percent of those questioned said they wanted Le Pen to become president, while 68 percent said they did not. But 75 percent said they would like to see far-right cabinet ministers, with 47 percent in favour of a National Front prime minister.
Fifty-six percent of respondents would like to see a National Front majority in parliament.
The poll, conducted by IFOP for Figaro-Magazine, questioned 403 people between March 14 and 19 who said they voted for the National Front at least once in the last 10 years.
Fully 93 percent of Le Pen supporters said they rejected fascism with 88 percent saying they favoured the ideals of the Republic. But 68 percent said they were nationalists.
The party will have its annual national congress in the French city of Strasbourg this weekend.
The poll found that a plurality of National Front voters were labourers and that most were between the ages of 25 and 64.
Thirty-three percent said France's record 12.7 unemployment was a main motivation supporting the National Front while 25 percent cited immigration.
